reported_failure: Simulation.reset() did not flush the dataset recorder's episode buffer, so twenty requested episodes of sixty steps were recorded as one episode of 1,140 frames; the reporter's earlier diagnosis blamed the policy

source_check.observed: reset() flushes the open recorder episode before mj_resetData; a failed flush returns an error instead of resetting into an undefined state (lines about 5656 to 5695)

explanations.genuine policy failure: the policy did not complete its episodes

decision_structure.cheapest_conventional_check: compare recorded episode count and frame count with the requested count (20 episodes, 60 steps): 1 episode and 1,140 frames identifies the recorder boundary failure without any policy analysis
decision_structure.published_remedy: auto-flush on reset (in the baseline's own tooling at main)
decision_structure.nisayon_addition: per-run execution receipts and reset events would show the same boundary failure; no additional decision follows

reasons: the cheapest ordinary check (count recorded episodes against requested episodes) settles the diagnosis; both procedures reach the same decision for the same work

no executable reproduction within bounds: the pre-fix revision, the MolmoAct policy weights, the simulation world and the private run logs named in the issue are not available public artifacts, and the weight download is out of scope
the source-level fact retained here (flush before reset at main) is not a reproduction of the failure
smallest_missing_artifact: a public pre-fix run record (dataset meta/info.json with total_episodes and total_frames) or a runnable minimal world plus a scripted policy; neither is needed to see that the count check decides the case
